hook.convey: one whole length (1 m, 1 cm) shared into 10 equal parts → each part is one tenth, written 1/10 or 0.1; the digit just after the point counts tenths; a ruler's small marks, a 1 m rope marked every 10 cm at the cricket pitch

point.en: This is a 1 metre strip, divided into 10 equal parts. One part is coloured: it is 1/10 of the metre, and as a decimal 1/10 is written 0.1, so 0.1 m. The first place after the point is the tenths place.

say.hi: Point ke theek baad wali jagah tenths ki hai: wahan ka har 1 grid ki ek poori row hai, yaani 10 chhote khaane. Agar wahan 0 ho, toh ek bhi poori row nahi, sirf doosri jagah wale chhote khaane.
say.en: The place right after the point is the tenths place: each 1 there is a full row of the grid, that is 10 small squares. If it holds 0, there is not one full row, only the small squares of the second place.

simpler.hi: Pehli jagah ka ank poori rows ginta hai, har row mein 10 khaane. Wahan 0 ho toh koi poori row nahi.
simpler.en: The first-place digit counts full rows of 10 squares each. A 0 there means no full row.

prompt.hi: Ek 10 × 10 grid par 0.06 rang karna hai. Kitne chhote khaane rangoge?
prompt.en: You must colour 0.06 on a 10 × 10 grid. How many small squares will you colour?

why.hi: 0.06 rang karna hai: tenths ki jagah 0, toh koi poori row nahi, aur 6 hundredths matlab 6 chhote khaane
why.en: To colour 0.06: the tenths place is 0, so no full row, and 6 hundredths means 6 small squares

simpler.hi: 0.06 mein tenths ki jagah dekho. Phir hundredths ki jagah ka ank gino.
simpler.en: Look at the tenths place of 0.06. Then count the digit in the hundredths place.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab yahi tenths aur hundredths units badalne mein kaam aayenge: centimetre se metre, millimetre se centimetre, aur paise se rupaye.
bridgeToNext.en: Next, these same tenths and hundredths help us change units: centimetres to metres, millimetres to centimetres, and paise to rupees.

simpler.hi: Ab tenths aur hundredths se units badalna seekhenge, jaise centimetre se metre. Board par ek number line zoom ki hui hai.
simpler.en: Now we use tenths and hundredths to change units, like centimetres to metres. On the board a number line is zoomed in.

hook.convey: 100 cm = 1 m and 100 paise = ₹1 → cm and paise sit in the hundredths place; 10 mm = 1 cm → mm sit in the tenths place of a cm; a car's length on a parking board, a price on a kitchen bill

use.hi: Ek car 4 m 35 cm lambi hai. Parking board par yahi lambai metre mein likhi jaati hai, kyunki 35 cm metre ke 35 hundredths hain.
use.en: A car is 4 m 35 cm long. On a parking board the same length is written in metres, because 35 cm is 35 hundredths of a metre.

use.hi: Kitchen ke saaman ka bill dekho: ₹1 mein 100 paise hote hain, isliye paise rupaye ke baad point ke aage do jagah mein likhe jaate hain.
use.en: Look at a bill for kitchen things: ₹1 has 100 paise, so paise are written in the two places after the point, following the rupees.

explain.convey: a height of 1 m 25 cm: 25 cm = 25 hundredths of a metre → 1.25 m on the zoomed line; adding cm adds hundredths → the child adds 5 cm and gets 1.3 m (not 1.75 m)

point.hi: Ek bachche ki oonchai 1 m 25 cm hai. 100 cm = 1 m, toh 25 cm metre ke 25 hundredths hain. Isliye 1 m 25 cm = 1.25 m, jo is line par 1 aur 2 ke beech hai.
point.en: A child's height is 1 m 25 cm. 100 cm = 1 m, so 25 cm is 25 hundredths of a metre. So 1 m 25 cm = 1.25 m, which is between 1 and 2 on this line.

prompt.hi: Is 1.25 m wali oonchai mein 5 cm aur jodo, toh nayi oonchai kitne metre hogi?
prompt.en: Add 5 cm to this height of 1.25 m. How many metres is the new height?

simpler.hi: Ek metre ke 100 cm hain, isliye har centimetre metre ka ek hundredth hai. 1 m 25 cm ko 1.25 m likhte hain.
simpler.en: A metre has 100 cm, so each centimetre is one hundredth of a metre. 1 m 25 cm is written 1.25 m.

explain.convey: 60 cm = 60 hundredths = 0.60 m, but 6 cm = 6 hundredths = 0.06 m: with fewer than 10 cm the tenths place holds 0 → the child adds 3 cm to 6 cm and writes 0.09 m (not 0.9 m)

point.hi: 60 cm metre ke 60 hundredths hain, yaani 0.60 m. Par 6 cm sirf 6 hundredths hain, isliye tenths ki jagah 0 aata hai aur 6 cm = 0.06 m.
point.en: 60 cm is 60 hundredths of a metre, that is 0.60 m. But 6 cm is only 6 hundredths, so the tenths place gets 0 and 6 cm = 0.06 m.

prompt.hi: Is 6 cm wale tukde mein 3 cm aur jodo, toh woh kitne metre ka hoga?
prompt.en: Add 3 cm to this 6 cm piece. How many metres long will it be?

why.hi: 6 + 3 = 9 cm, jo metre ke 9 hundredths hain, yaani 0.09 m
why.en: 6 + 3 = 9 cm, which is 9 hundredths of a metre, so 0.09 m

simpler.hi: 60 cm ho toh tenths ki jagah 6 aata hai: 0.60 m. Sirf 6 cm ho toh tenths ki jagah khaali rehti hai, wahan 0 likhte hain: 0.06 m.
simpler.en: With 60 cm the tenths place gets 6: 0.60 m. With only 6 cm the tenths place is empty, so we write 0 there: 0.06 m.

explain.convey: 1 cm = 10 equal mm → 1 mm = 1/10 cm = 0.1 cm: mm go in the tenths place of a cm, not the hundredths → the child writes 37 mm in cm

point.hi: 1 cm mein 10 barabar millimetre hote hain. Isliye 1 mm ek centimetre ka 1/10 hai, yaani 0.1 cm. Yahan millimetre, centimetre ka tenth hai, hundredth nahi.
point.en: 1 cm has 10 equal millimetres. So 1 mm is 1/10 of a centimetre, that is 0.1 cm. Here a millimetre is a tenth of a centimetre, not a hundredth.

prompt.hi: Ek keeda 37 mm lamba hai. Woh kitne centimetre ka hai?
prompt.en: An insect is 37 mm long. How many centimetres is it?

why.hi: 10 mm se 1 cm banta hai; 37 mm mein 3 poore centimetre aur 7 mm hain, yaani 3.7 cm
why.en: 10 mm make 1 cm; 37 mm holds 3 whole centimetres and 7 mm, that is 3.7 cm

simpler.hi: Das millimetre milkar ek centimetre banta hai. Toh ek millimetre, centimetre ka dasva hissa hai: 0.1 cm.
simpler.en: Ten millimetres make one centimetre. So one millimetre is a tenth of a centimetre: 0.1 cm.

explain.convey: ₹1 = 100 paise → 1 paisa = 1/100 rupee = ₹0.01: paise take the two places after the point, so a single-digit paise amount needs a 0 in the tenths place → the child reads ₹3.08 on a bill as ₹3 and 8 paise (not 80 paise)

point.hi: ₹1 mein 100 paise hote hain, toh 1 paisa ek rupaye ka 1/100 hai, yaani 0.01 rupaye. Isliye paise hamesha point ke baad ki do jagah lete hain.
point.en: ₹1 has 100 paise, so 1 paisa is 1/100 of a rupee, that is 0.01 rupees. That is why paise always take the two places after the point.

prompt.hi: Ek bill par 3.08 rupaye likha hai. Usme kitne rupaye aur kitne paise hain?
prompt.en: A bill shows 3.08 rupees. How many rupees and how many paise is that?

why.hi: Bill ke 3.08 rupaye mein point ke baad ki do jagah paise: 08 matlab 8 paise, point se pehle 3 rupaye
why.en: On the bill, the two places after the point in 3.08 rupees are paise: 08 is 8 paise, before it 3 rupees

simpler.hi: Ek rupaye mein sau paise, toh ek paisa sirf 0.01 rupaye hai. Isliye paise ke liye point ke baad do ank chahiye.
simpler.en: A rupee has a hundred paise, so one paisa is just 0.01 rupees. So paise need two digits after the point.

problem.hi: Ek almaari 2 m 7 cm oonchi hai, aur 1 m mein 100 cm hote hain. Uski oonchai sirf metre mein, decimal se likho.
problem.en: A cupboard is 2 m 7 cm tall, and 1 m has 100 cm. Write its height in metres only, as a decimal.

simpler.hi: 1 m mein 100 cm hote hain, toh 7 cm ek metre ke 100 hisson mein se 7 hisse hain. Ise decimal mein do jagah tak likhna hai.
simpler.en: 1 m has 100 cm, so 7 cm is 7 of the 100 parts of a metre. Write it as a decimal with two places.

givens.en: the cupboard is 2 m 7 cm tall

find.en: the height in metres, as a decimal

why.hi: 100 barabar centimetre milkar 1 metre banate hain
why.en: 100 equal centimetres make 1 metre

simpler.hi: Sau centimetre jodo toh ek metre banta hai. Isliye 1 cm metre ka 1/100 hai, yaani 0.01 m.
simpler.en: Put a hundred centimetres together and you get one metre. So 1 cm is 1/100 of a metre, that is 0.01 m.

why.hi: har centimetre metre ka ek hundredth hai
why.en: each centimetre is one hundredth of a metre

simpler.hi: Ek centimetre metre ke sau hisson mein se ek hai. Toh 7 cm metre ka 7/100 hai, yaani 0.07 m.
simpler.en: One centimetre is one of a metre's hundred parts. So 7 cm is 7/100 of a metre, that is 0.07 m.

why.hi: 7 cm mein ek bhi poora tenth yaani 10 cm nahi hai
why.en: 7 cm does not hold even one whole tenth, that is 10 cm

simpler.hi: 7 cm mein ek poora tenth bhi nahi banta. Isliye tenths ki jagah 0 aata hai.
simpler.en: 7 cm does not make even one whole tenth. So the tenths place gets 0.

prompt.hi: Ab 2 m aur 0.07 m ko saath likho. Almaari kitne metre oonchi hai?
prompt.en: Now put 2 m and 0.07 m together. How many metres tall is the cupboard?

simpler.hi: Poore 2 m point se pehle likho. Phir point ke baad 0.07 wale digits likho.
simpler.en: Write the 2 whole metres before the point. Then write the digits of 0.07 after the point.

why.hi: almaari 2 m 7 cm hai, aur 7 cm yaani 0.07 m, toh 2 + 0.07 = 2.07 m

answer.hi: almaari 2 m 7 cm yaani 2.07 m oonchi hai
answer.en: the cupboard is 2 m 7 cm, that is 2.07 m, tall

why.hi: 7 cm sirf 7 hundredths metre hai, isliye 7 point ke baad doosri jagah par aata hai, tenths ki jagah 0
why.en: 7 cm is only 7 hundredths of a metre, so 7 goes second after the point and the tenths place is 0

prompt.hi: Ek pauda ek hafte mein 3 cm bada hua. Yeh badhat kitne metre hai?
prompt.en: A plant grew 3 cm in a week. How many metres is this growth?

why.hi: badhat 3 cm hai, aur 1 m = 100 cm, toh 3 cm metre ke 3 hundredths hain: 0.03 m
why.en: the growth is 3 cm, and 1 m = 100 cm, so 3 cm is 3 hundredths of a metre: 0.03 m

simpler.hi: 3 cm metre ke sirf 3 hundredths hain. Socho, tenths ki jagah par kya aayega.
simpler.en: 3 cm is only 3 hundredths of a metre. Think what goes in the tenths place.

prompt.hi: Ek toffee ka daam ₹1 aur 6 paise hai, par dukaandaar ne 1.6 rupaye likh diye. Usne kitne paise zyada likhe?
prompt.en: A toffee costs ₹1 and 6 paise, but the shopkeeper wrote 1.6 rupees. How many paise too much did he write?

why.hi: likhe 1.6 rupaye matlab ₹1 aur 60 paise, sahi daam ₹1 aur 6 paise, toh 60 − 6 = 54 paise zyada
why.en: the 1.6 rupees written is ₹1 and 60 paise, right price ₹1 and 6 paise: 60 − 6 = 54 paise more

simpler.hi: Socho board wale daam mein kitne paise hain, aur sahi daam mein kitne. Phir dono ka farak nikaalo.
simpler.en: Think how many paise the price on the board has, and how many the right price has. Then find the difference.

prompt.hi: Darzi ke paas 2.6 m kapda tha. Usne usme se 6 cm kaat diya. Ab kitne metre kapda bacha?
prompt.en: A tailor had 2.6 m of cloth. He cut 6 cm off it. How many metres of cloth are left now?

why.hi: Kapda 2.6 m = 260 cm tha, 6 cm kaata, toh 260 − 6 = 254 cm, yaani 2.54 m bacha
why.en: The cloth was 2.6 m = 260 cm; cut 6 cm, and 260 − 6 = 254 cm = 2.54 m

simpler.hi: Pehle 2.6 m ko centimetre mein badlo, kyunki kaata hua tukda centimetre mein hai. Phir ghatao aur wapas metre mein likho.
simpler.en: First change 2.6 m into centimetres, since the cut piece is in centimetres. Then subtract and write it back in metres.

ladder.why: first straight use: a height of 1 m 45 cm → 1.45 m
₹3 and 5 paise → ₹3.05, the 0 that holds the tenths place
error-spot: 8 cm written as 0.8 m → it is 0.08 m, and 0.8 m would be 80 cm
far transfer: two sports-day jumps, 3 m 8 cm against 3.8 m → who jumped further, by 72 cm

remediation.move: metre strip marked in cm: 1 m is 100 cm, not 10, so each cm is a hundredth of a metre and each tenth of a metre is 10 cm → turn 0.4 m back into cm

say.hi: 1 metre mein 100 cm hote hain, 10 nahi. Isliye har centimetre metre ka ek hundredth hai, aur metre ka har tenth das centimetre ka hota hai.
say.en: 1 metre has 100 cm, not 10. So each centimetre is one hundredth of a metre, and each tenth of a metre is ten centimetres.

simpler.hi: Metre ke sau centimetre hain. Ek centimetre metre ka sauvaan hissa hai, aur dasva hissa das centimetre.
simpler.en: There are a hundred centimetres in a metre. One centimetre is a hundredth of a metre, and a tenth is ten centimetres.

prompt.hi: Ek rassi 0.4 m lambi hai. Woh kitne centimetre ki hai?
prompt.en: A rope is 0.4 m long. How many centimetres is it?

why.hi: Rassi 0.4 m = 4 tenths metre, aur metre ka har tenth 10 cm hai, toh 4 × 10 = 40 cm
why.en: The rope is 0.4 m, 4 tenths of a metre; each tenth is 10 cm, so 4 × 10 = 40 cm

simpler.hi: 0.4 m mein kitne dasve hisse hain, gino. Har dasva hissa kitne centimetre ka hai, socho.
simpler.en: Count how many tenths 0.4 m has. Think how many centimetres each tenth is.

remediation.move: paise fill two places after the point: the first counts tens of paise, the second single paise → compare ₹3.5 (₹3 and 50 paise) with ₹3.05 (₹3 and 5 paise)

say.hi: Paise ko rupaye mein likhne par point ke baad ki dono jagah bharti hain, kyunki ek rupaye mein sau paise hote hain. Point ke theek baad wala ank das-das paise ginta hai, aur doosra ank akele paise.
say.en: When paise are written in rupees, both places after the point fill up, because one rupee has a hundred paise. The digit right after the point counts tens of paise, and the second digit counts single paise.

simpler.hi: Point ke baad pehla ank das paise ke jhund ginta hai. Doosra ank akele paise ginta hai.
simpler.en: After the point, the first digit counts bunches of ten paise. The second digit counts single paise.

prompt.hi: Pen ka daam 3.5 rupaye hai aur pencil ka 3.05 rupaye. Kaunsi cheez mehngi hai, pen ya pencil?
prompt.en: The pen costs 3.5 rupees and the pencil 3.05 rupees. Which costs more, the pen or the pencil?

why.hi: Pen ke 3.5 rupaye matlab ₹3 aur 50 paise, pencil ke 3.05 rupaye sirf ₹3 aur 5 paise, toh pen mehnga hai
why.en: The pen's 3.5 rupees is ₹3 and 50 paise, the pencil's 3.05 rupees just ₹3 and 5 paise: the pen costs more

simpler.hi: Dono daam ko rupaye aur paise mein todkar dekho.
simpler.en: Split both prices into rupees and paise and look.
